correctness.rationale: Direct kick-drift-kick calculation gives determinant one and a positive fixed-h preserved metric for 0<h<2. Symbolically tr(ABA^-1B^-1)-2=a²b²(a-b)²(a+b)²/16, strictly positive for distinct support values. The subgroup is noncompact; ellipticity eliminates invariant one-line and two-line sets except an impossible common h=sqrt(2), and any finite set of at least three lines would make the projective group finite, contradicting the hyperbolic commutator. Every non-point-mass law has such two support values, giving total irreducibility of its full generated group. Bounded M(h) and inverses give integrability, so Furstenberg yields a.s. positive norm exponent, and SLLN yields the physical-time exponent. For point masses a fixed SPD invariant form bounds powers. Exact symbolic and rational replay verifies all nonstandard algebra; no finite computation is mistaken for the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Inspected prescribed/periodic timestep analyses, general random-product criterion, and random-shear literature do not supply the specific all-distribution classification for iid stable-range velocity-Verlet steps. Published symplectic-Euler random-step work addresses a different first-order matrix and mean-square energy, not the almost-sure exponent of this second-order scheme. The contribution proves exact hyperbolic commutator and total irreducibility for every distinct pair, which activates Furstenberg for any non-point-mass step law; the generic theorem alone does not verify its numerical-method hypotheses. Specialist precedence remains a risk.
residual_risks: Potential specialist precedent applying the classic Furstenberg criterion to randomized velocity Verlet with the same all-distribution statement may not be indexed in the consulted sources.

value.rationale: Random time-step selection is a natural version of the well-documented variable-step stability problem for long-time symplectic integration. The result gives a complete qualitative stability classification for the canonical second-order velocity-Verlet scheme under every exogenous iid stable-step law: arbitrary nonzero jitter causes almost-sure exponential top-norm growth, even for pairs whose deterministic alternation is bounded. This is a nontrivial structural classification with a clear numerical-analysis diagnostic; it is not only an isolated toy computation, a renamed Euler expected-moment result, or an unmotivated parameter slice. It does not claim a rate estimate, generic nonlinear dynamics, or practical runtime gain.
